This question is part of the benchmark eval corpus. According to the reference answer in `/Users/admin/Projects/sweet-search-private/eval/agent-eval/questions/fastify.jsonl` (line 1):

> The `VERSION` constant is defined at **line 3 of `fastify.js`** as:
> ```js
> const VERSION = '5.8.4'
> ```

The `applicationHooks` array is defined at **lines 3–10** of `lib/hooks.js`:

```js
const applicationHooks = [
  'onRoute',
  'onRegister',
  'onReady',
  'onListen',
  'preClose',
  'onClose'
]
```

These 6 hooks are distinct from the `lifecycleHooks` (lines 11–22). They are concatenated together into `supportedHooks` at line 23. Notably, `onClose` appears in the `applicationHooks` array but is **not** initialized as an array property in the `Hooks` constructor (lines 40–56) — only `onRoute`, `onRegister`, `onReady`, `onListen`, and `preClose` get array slots there.

Fastify registers exactly **two** default content-type parsers, set up in the `ContentTypeParser` constructor at **`lib/content-type-parser.js` lines 37–38**:

| Content-Type | Parser | `parseAs` |
|---|---|---|
| `application/json` | `defaultJsonParser` (via `secure-json-parse`) | string (UTF-8) |
| `text/plain` | `defaultPlainTextParser` (returns body as-is) | string (UTF-8) |

**Details:**

1. **`application/json`** (line 37) — uses `getDefaultJsonParser()` which wraps [`secure-json-parse`](https://github.com/nicolo-ribaudo/secure-json-parse) with proto/constructor poisoning protection (configurable via `onProtoPoisoning` / `onConstructorPoisoning` options). Throws `FST_ERR_CTP_EMPTY_JSON_BODY` for empty bodies, `FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_JSON_BODY` for invalid JSON.

2. **`text/plain`** (line 38) — uses `defaultPlainTextParser` (line 324), which simply calls `done(null, body)` — a passthrough that returns the raw body string.

Both are registered with `asString: true` (parsed as UTF-8 string before the handler fn is called).

**No wildcard/catch-all parser is registered by default.** If a request arrives with an unrecognized `Content-Type`, Fastify replies with `FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_MEDIA_TYPE` (line 195). You can register a catch-all with `fastify.addContentTypeParser('*', ...)`.

**Location:** `lib/noop-set.js`, line 3 (in the fastify repo at `eval/repos/fastify/lib/noop-set.js`)

**What it does:** `noopSet()` returns a fake/stub object that has the same interface as a native `Set` but does nothing:

| Method/Property | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `add()` | No-op — discards the value |
| `delete()` | No-op — does nothing |
| `has()` | Always returns `true` |
| `[Symbol.iterator]` | Returns an empty generator (yields nothing) |

**Why it exists:** It's used in `lib/server.js` (line 139) as a drop-in replacement for a real `Set` when connection tracking isn't needed:

```js
const keepAliveConnections = !serverHasCloseAllConnections && forceCloseConnections === true
  ? new Set()
  : noopSet()
```

When `forceCloseConnections` is not `true` (or the server already has `closeAllConnections`), there's no need to actually track keep-alive connections, so `noopSet()` is used to avoid the overhead of a real `Set` while keeping the rest of the code path uniform — all calls to `.add()`, `.delete()`, etc. still work without branching.

The `.borp.yaml` at `eval/repos/fastify/.borp.yaml` specifies two file patterns under the `files` key:

- `test/**/*.test.js`
- `test/**/*.test.mjs`

Both match any `.test.js` or `.test.mjs` files anywhere under the `test/` directory tree.

Fastify classifies **`GET`**, **`HEAD`**, and **`TRACE`** as bodyless by default.

This is defined in **`fastify.js` line 132–137** as a `Set` stored on `kSupportedHTTPMethods.bodyless`:

```js
bodyless: new Set([
  // Standard
  'GET',
  'HEAD',
  'TRACE'
]),
```

**Practical implications:**
- In `lib/handle-request.js:29`, body parsing is **skipped** for these methods.
- In `lib/route.js:619`, defining a `schema.body` on a bodyless route triggers a **warning/error**.
- Custom methods can be moved in/out of the bodyless set at runtime via `this[kSupportedHTTPMethods].bodyless.add(method)` / `.delete(method)` (`fastify.js:807–810`).

**`Reply.prototype.status` is defined at line 335 of `/Users/admin/Projects/sweet-search-private/eval/repos/fastify/lib/reply.js`** — it's a direct alias for `Reply.prototype.code`:

```js
Reply.prototype.status = Reply.prototype.code
```

The actual implementation is `Reply.prototype.code` (lines 324–333):

```js
Reply.prototype.code = function (code) {
  const statusCode = +code
  if (!(statusCode >= 100 && statusCode <= 599)) {
    throw new FST_ERR_BAD_STATUS_CODE(code || String(code))
  }
  this.raw.statusCode = statusCode
  this[kReplyHasStatusCode] = true
  return this
}
```

**What it does:**
1. Coerces `code` to a number with `+code`.
2. Validates it's in the range **100–599**; throws `FST_ERR_BAD_STATUS_CODE` otherwise.
3. Sets `this.raw.statusCode` (the underlying Node.js `http.ServerResponse`) to the validated value.
4. Marks `kReplyHasStatusCode = true` (used elsewhere, e.g. to pick the default redirect code in `redirect()`).
5. Returns `this` for chaining.

`reply.status(200)` and `reply.code(200)` are **identical** — `status` is purely an alias for Express-style familiarity.

When a request body exceeds the configured `bodyLimit`, the error code is **`FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE`**, which maps to HTTP **`413`** (Payload Too Large).

**Defined in** `lib/errors.js`, lines 105–110:
```js
FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE: createError(
  'FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE',
  'Request body is too large',
  413,
  RangeError
),
```

It's a `RangeError` subclass with `statusCode: 413`. You can also see it documented in `docs/Reference/Errors.md` line 303 under the content-type-parser section.

`defaultSchemaErrorFormatter` is defined in **`lib/context.js` at line 87**:

```js
function defaultSchemaErrorFormatter (errors, dataVar) {

  ...
}
```

It's also referenced at line 75 as the fallback formatter in the `Context` constructor, used when neither a route-level `schemaErrorFormatter` nor a server-level `kSchemaErrorFormatter` is provided.

Five warning codes are defined in `lib/warnings.js` (all via `process-warning`'s `createWarning`):

| Code | Name | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| **FSTWRN001** | `FastifyWarning` | Missing schema for a route — `'The %s schema for %s: %s is missing.'` (line 16) |
| **FSTWRN003** | `FastifyWarning` | Handler mixes async and callback styles — risk of unhandled rejections (line 23) |
| **FSTWRN004** | `FastifyWarning` | `errorHandler` overridden in the same scope — may cause subtle bugs (line 30) |
| **FSTSEC001** | `FastifySecurity` | Content-Type RegExp may be vulnerable to CORS attack — missing `^` or `;?` (line 37) |
| **FSTDEP022** | `FastifyWarning` | Deprecation — direct router options property access; use `options.routerOptions` instead; removed in Fastify v6 (line 44) |

Note the comment at the top (lines 7–13): codes `FSTDEP001`–`FSTDEP021` and `FSTWRN001`–`FSTWRN002` were used by v4 and **must not be reused**; `FSTDEP022` is the sole v5 deprecation code.
